title: Coulomb's Law

references.label: NCERT Physics Part I, Class 12 — Electric Charges and Fields

explanation: Coulomb's law describes the electrostatic force between two point charges: proportional to the product of the charges and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them, exactly mirroring the mathematical form of Newton's law of gravitation. Like charges repel; unlike charges attract — the sign of the charges determines the direction, while the magnitude comes from the formula. Result is expressed in N (newton). Conditions/assumptions: Strictly applies to point charges (or spherically symmetric charge distributions treated as points); assumes a vacuum/air unless a medium's permittivity is specified

variables.meaning: Magnitudes of the two point charges

workedExample.scenario: Two point charges of +2 μC and +3 μC are 0.5 m apart.
workedExample.result: F ≈ 0.216 N (repulsive, since both charges are positive)

commonMistakes: Forgetting to convert charge units (μC, nC) to coulombs before substituting.
Ignoring the medium — the formula's constant k changes if the charges are in a dielectric medium rather than vacuum/air.
genZNote: Coulomb's law: same shape as gravity's formula, just with charges instead of masses.
